summary: Susanne Mrozik specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an M.T.S. at Harvard University, studying under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. Her career includes posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushanta Sen worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After studying at Visva-Bharati University, he served there as a lecturer in 1986 and later became a Lecturer in Indian Religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Indologist Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS, and University of Bonn. He held posts at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, University of Dhaka (~1923–1947), Jadavpur University, University of London, and Sanskrit College and University.
Susmita Basu Majumdar works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she later held a post around 2002.

Susumu Kajiura (b. 1957) is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and headed the humanities research laboratory at Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property in 2001.

Susumu Otake (b. 1974) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied under Makio Takemura at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) and held part-time lecturing posts at Kyoto University (~2008), Hanazono University (attested 2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (attested 2012–2013).

Susumu Shimazono (b. 1948) is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and later held posts at Sophia University.

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University, University of Paris, and Kyoto University under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as a professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri (b. 1936) works in Buddhist studies. Educated at Nalanda College, University of London, University of Pennsylvania, and University of Toronto, he founded and served as president of Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, alongside holding posts at Toronto and Ontario Tech.

Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at EFEO, was the first curator of Cambodia's National Library, and became the first secretary-general of the Buddhist Institute.

Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at Cambridge, LSE, the Information Network Focus on Religious Movements, Open University, and King's College London.

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his education through studies at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.
Sven Sellmer is an Indologist working in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933, taught scholars including Alexis Sanderson and Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, and founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He founded the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha, and served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980).
Swami Satyananda Puri (1902–1942) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1920–1926), where he later held an academic post.

Swami Siddheswarananda (1897–1957) was active in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and was affiliated with the Ramakrishna Order from around 1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda (1872–1908) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He was educated at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.

Swami Vishnudevananda (1927–1993) was active in religious studies and Indology. He was a disciple of Sivananda Saraswati from around 1947 to 1957 and founded the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.
